//: ONE rule set, TWO implementations, and this file is what stops them drifting.
//why: Plugins\WebSocket\Domain\Channel (PHP) is the original; edge/internal/channel (Go) exists because the edge must refuse a malformed name BEFORE spending a NATS round trip asking PHP about it — otherwise an unauthenticated client chooses how much work the application does, which is a denial-of-service primitive. Two implementations of a security rule drift silently: the stricter one refuses what the other allows, and whichever side a deployment happens to run decides what is reachable. Both test suites read THIS file, so a change made to one implementation and not the other fails on one of them.
//adding: Add a vector here FIRST, watch both suites fail, then change both implementations.
//control-bytes: Not listed above because JSON cannot carry a raw NUL. Both suites generate every byte 0x00-0x1F plus 0x7F in a name and assert refusal, which is the case PHP's default trim() silently REPAIRED into a valid channel before it was pinned.
//length: Both suites assert 128 bytes is accepted and 129 refused, generated rather than listed.
